extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, patent examiners, and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and rules governing patent re-issue: what a re-issue may or may not claim, evidence and timing requirements (inadvertence, delay), identity with the original, procedural/formal requirements, effects on rights, and Patent Office and court treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue limited to matters original attempted to claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot cover what the original might have claimed but only what the original attempted to claim; improper to embrace matters described but not attempted to be claimed in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the original specification/claims/drawings/models to determine what the original attempted to claim; do not add subject-matter that was merely suggested or described without any attempt to claim it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot claim matter merely claimed but not described
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot cover what is merely claimed but not described in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in the original that lack supporting description cannot be used as a basis to expand a re-issue; supporting description (specification, drawings, model) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot cover matter courts deem not described in original
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot cover matters which the courts have held not described in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial determinations about sufficiency of the original specification restrict allowable re-issue subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: May cover inventions original attempted to describe and claim (joinder rules permitting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may cover all the inventions which the original attempted to describe and claim, if the rules of joinder permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the original attempted to set forth multiple inventions, re-issue can claim them provided joinder/separability rules are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: May claim what original shows it attempted to protect
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may claim whatever the original patent itself shows that it attempted to protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the original patent as a whole to infer the patentee's attempt to protect particular subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: May cover matter necessarily implied from original description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may cover matter necessarily implied from the Description and Claims of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inferences that are necessary and inevitable from the original disclosure may be included in a re-issue even if not explicitly claimed, subject to identity and other limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: May cover matter outside judicial interpretation of original claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may cover matter not within the judicial interpretation of the original claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original text supports broader subject-matter than prior judicial construction recognized, a re-issue may claim that subject-matter (still subject to other constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: May cover inventions inseparably connected with original invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may cover all inventions inseparably connected with the one claimed in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where inventions are inseparably connected, a re-issue can extend to those connected inventions if they were attempted to be described/claimed originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of subject-matter presumed until contrary appears
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of subject-matter with that of the original is presumed until the contrary appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The default presumption favors identity; challenger bears burden to show divergence between original and re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity depends on things described, not on descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity depends on the things described, not on the descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance over form: consider the actual subject-matter (structure, elements, functions), not merely differences in wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity determined by what original actually set forth
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity is determined by what the original did set forth, not by what it might have set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not speculate about unrealized or hypothetical disclosures; rely on the original's concrete content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity primarily a question of interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity with the original is primarily a question of interpretation, not of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts interpret specifications/claims (with reference to the state of the art at the time) to determine identity; extrinsic evidence is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity ascertained by comparing specifications, drawings, models
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity is ascertained by comparing specifications, drawings, and models of original and re-issue all together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full documentary comparison (including models) is used; no single part controls if others show identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity cannot be shown by extrinsic or parol proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity cannot be shown by extrinsic evidence or by parol proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of identity must rest on the original written specification/drawings/models and re-issue documents, not on extrinsic oral testimony except in limited circumstances (e.g., lost model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to determine what original attempted to describe and claim
rubrics_metrics.description: What the original attempted to describe and claim is ascertained from the original specification itself compared with the actual invention and the re-issue specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare original document(s) to the actual invention and the proposed re-issue; the mode of determining attempt may appear in specification, drawings, or model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot cover matter not found in original spec/drawings/model
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue can cover nothing which is not found in the original specification, drawings, or model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced in re-issue; any departure must be traceable to matter present in the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attempt to describe/claim may appear in specification, drawings, or model
rubrics_metrics.description: The attempt of the original to describe and claim may appear either in the specification, drawings, or model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect all parts of the original record to locate any indication the inventor sought to claim particular subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: In comparing original and re-issue both construed by state of the art at original application date
rubrics_metrics.description: In comparing original and re-issue both are construed by the state of the art at the date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation is objective and anchored to the knowledge and terminology of the relevant art when the original was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue whose only claims are not in original is void
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue whose only claims are not in the original is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim in the re-issue lacks basis in the original, the re-issue is invalid; at least some claims must be traceable to the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption original intended to claim all properly claimable under its description
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a presumption that the original intended to claim all that could properly have been claimed under its description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption supports some latitude in re-issue, but it is rebuttable by evidence of intentional exclusion or other limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may amend patent to any extent necessary to secure the invention attempted in original
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may amend the patent to any extent necessary to secure the invention attempted to be described and claimed in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted amendments include clarifying language, correcting errors, and making definite what was previously inferential — but not adding new subject-matter beyond what was attempted originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may vary in language, description, mode of making/use, claims count/scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may vary from the original in language, in general description, in statements of mode of making and use, in number and scope of claims, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variations in form and drafting are allowed so long as identity of subject-matter with the original is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: May make definite what was previously matter of inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may make definite what was before matter of inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible to convert implied disclosures into explicit claim language where original disclosure supports the inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: May enlarge or narrow claims but enlargement is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may enlarge or narrow claims, but cannot enlarge the patent or claims beyond permitted bounds; re-issue expressly enlarging claims is void as against the public and intervening rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlargements that affect third parties' rights or go beyond what was attempted in the original are defective; narrowings are generally acceptable but must not be used to improperly manipulate rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: May enlarge claims when original inoperative due to narrowness
rubrics_metrics.description: May enlarge claims when the original is inoperative from narrowness of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original claim language rendered the patent inoperative as to the real invention, re-issue to enlarge claims may be allowed to secure the invention, subject to diligence and other constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic vs specific: scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic patent may cover all included species; cannot claim different species from the one claimed in the original; a specific patent cannot cover the genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not broaden a specific claim to a genus in re-issue; conversely, generic-to-specific coverage is permissible if supported by the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-patent re-issue limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A combination-patent cannot re-issue to cover a combination of less than all the elements, or of different elements, or of the same elements differently combined; may claim as a combination what the original claimed as an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue cannot create claims to subcombinations inconsistent with original disclosure unless conditions for subcombinations are satisfied and not barred by delay/intervening rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: May omit non-essentials or substitute equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may omit non-essentials or substitute equivalents; may cover elements when the original described them or equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted to streamline claims by removing non-essential elements or by claiming equivalents, provided the original supports such treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue not allowed unless defect arose from inadvertence/accident/mistake and without fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue is not allowed unless the defect arose through inadvertence, accident, or mistake and without fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Inadvertence," "accident," and "mistake" relate to the application, not to the invention; fraud and intentional defects are not remedied by re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue is prima facie evidence of inadvertence
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue is prima facie evidence of inadvertence, accident, or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant's oath and filing create a presumption of inadvertence which opponents may rebut with evidence of intentional exclusion or other proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot amend defects arising through fraud; intentional defects not amendable
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot amend defects arising through fraud; intentional defects not amendable even if not fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a defect was intentional is determined by the patent, Patent Office records, or applicant's acts/omissions before or after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot restore matter intentionally excluded or rejected with acquiescence
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot restore matter intentionally excluded from the original claims, nor can it cover matter disclaimed or rejected in the Patent Office with the patentee's acquiescence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentional disclaimers and examiner rejections agreed to by the patentee bar re-claiming that subject-matter in re-issue, though restoration may be possible where exclusion resulted from mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may restore matter disclaimed by mistake in PTO or by attorney without authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may restore matter disclaimed through a mistake in the Patent Office or by an attorney without authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is limited and requires proof of the mistake and that the original exclusion was not intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of intentional exclusion from failure to claim is prima facie only
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumption of intentional exclusion from failure to claim clearly described matter is prima facie only and may be rebutted, especially if amendment is made without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context, timing, and subsequent conduct determine whether omission was intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay and diligence rules: unreasonable delay can bar re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay in applying for re-issue, if apparent on its face, raises a question of law as to validity; diligence is required; less than two years' delay may be unreasonable; two years' delay unreasonable unless explained; no fixed rule, court examines circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both delay in discovering a defect and delay in acting can be unreasonable; ignorance of law does not excuse delay; special rules and examples apply (no simple bright-line rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreasonable delay may show intentional exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Unreasonable delay in amending shows that there was no inadvertence, accident, or mistake; intentional exclusion may be inferred from undue delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness of the re-issue filing relative to when the patentee knew or should have known of the defect is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to re-issue not affected by matters occurring after original issue; but intervening rights matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to re-issue is not affected by matters occurring after issue of the original; however intervening rights (conduct of third parties) affect right to re-issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-issuance events may be evidence of facts existing at the original date but cannot generally defeat a re-issue unless intervening rights have vested or delay prejudiced others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue construed to sustain it if possible; otherwise invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue is to be construed, if possible, to sustain it; but it is invalid unless it can be so construed by reference to the original and the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will seek an interpretation consistent with validity, but where divergence from the original is evident, the re-issue may be void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and succession of re-issues: not limited; each stands alone
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of re-issues is not limited by law; several successive re-issues are allowable; each is presumed necessary to cure defects and stands by itself free from the defects of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple re-issues are permissible, but each must independently satisfy the rules (no new matter, inadvertence where required, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional re-issues allowed when inventions separable
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisions (divisional re-issues) are allowable and proper when inventions are separable; each division must cover a patentable invention and must issue to the same patentee for parts embraced in the original invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A division may describe the whole invention but must claim only its own part; divisions are separate patents and may supersede the original upon surrender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue effects on rights and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue supersedes the original and requires its surrender; it takes effect on grant of the re-issue; it suspends at once all rights of action and no damages for infringements prior to re-issue are recoverable (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should note that re-issue changes the basis for infringement suits and can affect past and future remedies; surrender and timing have significant consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for re-issue and consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Who must apply for re-issue: inventor (if living) must concur, even if he has assigned the patent; re-issue to patentee bars a re-issue to an unrecorded assignee; executor may obtain re-issue; assignees' consent shown by abstract of title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper parties join and consent; applications by or for assignees must respect assignment formalities and recorded rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form, oath, and contents; specification must follow original language except as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for re-issue requires oath and contents; the specification, drawings, and model must be submitted; specification must follow language of original unless departure is necessary; drawings cannot vary unless the variation appears in the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft re-issue specifications closely tied to the original language and record; departures should be justified by necessity to cure defects or clarify, not to introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office examination powers over re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office has the same power over re-issue as over the original: examination as to patentability, identity with original, and fact of inadvertence, etc.; patentability is determined by the state of the art at date of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect substantive examination, not a rubber stamp; original grant does not guarantee allowance of re-issue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity may be shown in PTO when no drawings or model; extrinsic evidence limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity with the original may be shown in the Patent Office when there are no drawings or model; extrinsic evidence admissible only in limited circumstances (e.g., lost model, incorrect drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where documentary gaps exist, PTO and courts allow limited extrinsic proof but require the clearest evidence to change drawings/models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may restore rejected claim if later allowed to another applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may restore a claim that was rejected in the Patent Office with the acquiescence of the patentee if it has since been allowed to another applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration depends on intervening events and equities; mere earlier rejection with acquiescence usually bars restoration absent subsequent allowance to another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers in re-issue bind patentee but do not estop future re-issue unless excluded from original
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclaimers in a re-issue bind the patentee in suits on that re-issue, but do not estop him from claiming the same matter in a new re-issue unless it was excluded from the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A re-issue disclaimer has immediate effect for that grant, but may not be an absolute bar against future action unless tied to the original patent's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot avoid consequences of improper PTO rejection; appeals required
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue cannot avert the consequences of an improper rejection in the Patent Office; parties must appeal or sue in equity rather than rely on re-issue to correct PTO error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PTO rejection harmed rights, seek direct PTO appeal or judicial relief rather than use re-issue as a cure-all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may be invalidated if applicant attempted fraud or was not true inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue is void if the applicant attempted fraud (e.g., knew at date of application he was not the true inventor); re-issue can be attacked for fraudulent specification or fraud in defects of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good faith and correct inventorship are prerequisites; allegations of fraud will expose the re-issue to collateral attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue does not affect judgments or closed transactions based on the original
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue does not affect judgments, payments, or any closed transactions based on the original patent; rights under the re-issue are governed by the same law as under the original and by contracts made as to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing contractual and adjudicated rights tied to the original patent remain protected despite a later re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of re-issue may be shown by acquiescence; re-issue after contest has presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of a re-issue may be shown by acquiescence in the original; a re-issue granted after a severe contest has a strong presumption in its favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of prior acquiescence or a contested allowance history can influence judicial deference to a re-issue's validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue date and term; effect of acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue takes effect on grant of the re-issue; accepting the surrender and allowing a re-issue is final as to date of the invention (and date-related issues) and, to an extent, as to inadvertence and good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTO's acceptance has final effects on certain issues (e.g., date of invention), but some matters (fraud, patentability) remain open to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may be dismissed if original on its face was void
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue may be dismissed if on its face the original was void (e.g., for want of patentability or priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original patent lacks fundamental statutory requirements, a re-issue cannot redeem it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender and surrender-withdrawal procedures and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrender of the original is required for re-issue; withdrawal and revocation of surrender and hearing rights exist; surrender made effective by ratification; surrender destroys certain existing rights once accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural formalities around surrender are consequential—surrender accepted by PTO can extinguish pre-existing rights of action and requires careful client counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model/drawings: lost model proof and restrictions on change
rubrics_metrics.description: Original model may be inspected by the court; lost model must be proved; when a model is lost and drawings are incorrect they cannot be changed without the clearest evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alterations to drawings/models in re-issue are disfavored absent very strong proof; lost-model proofs are exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may cover matter previously described but impracticable
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue may cover matter which as previously described was impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior impracticability does not necessarily bar inclusion in re-issue if original description supports it and other re-issue prerequisites are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquiescence and estoppel implications of re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue accepted and relied upon may estop challengers and has evidentiary weight; however, re-issue cannot be used to overreach the public or intervening patentees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts weigh public reliance and intervening rights when evaluating re-issue equities.
